PROCEDURE CODE
1154 
In the cases provided for in Article 1151, 2¡, the Justice of the Peace may decide not to affix the seals where the value of the furnishings of the estate found in the place where he is proceeding does not exceed ((EUR 1,240)) according to his estimate. 
If he does not affix the seals, the Justice of the Peace draws up a descriptive statement of the movable property as well as the cash and securities found at the place where he proceeds and entrusts them to a curator whom he designates at the bottom of his report.
The curator has the powers and obligations listed in Article [1 4.58, ¤ 2,]1 of the Civil
Code, but only in respect of the cash, furniture and securities found in the residence of the deceased where the Justice of the Peace proceeded.
However, he is not obliged to have an inventory drawn up and he may sell all or part of the objects entrusted to him, either by public auction or by mutual agreement, on expiry of a period of forty days from the date of his appointment. This period may be reduced by the Justice of the Peace.
The curator's powers cease when heirs or universal legatees accepting the estate have made themselves known.
